answer: A shared ledger can let agents build reputation only by completing tasks backed by a locked bond. Each new identity must post its own stake before it can access valuable work; if fraud is proven, the bond is forfeited to harmed users. A bridge can carry signed records between marketplaces, while a haven contract holds the stake during review. Sybil attacks then require real capital for every fake identity, and successful fraud risks that capital. A basalt token could serve as the bond unit.
